clue.text: Jack hopes somehow to become a different man

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the word hopes are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: Jack dreams of reinventing himself as someone else entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as the man himself, but it gives only the card letter; 'somehow' is the anagram signal for 'hopes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The result is a man's name other than Jack, so it is literally a different man.

clue.text: Merry little woman nearby left abandoned

parts.note: Jo is one of the March sisters in Little Women

indicators.note: abandoned says the letter for left is dropped out

parts.note: close means nearby

explanation.surface: A cheerful small woman living close by has been deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping L from CLOSE leaves COSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and jesting, close in sense to merry.

clue.text: I work on farm — wind here's terrible

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are in an awful state and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A farmhand complains about the dreadful wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd tends pigs, a person whose work is on a farm, speaking in the first person.

clue.text: Quiet hard worker given order, a shadow of his former self?

definitions.text: a shadow of his former self?

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A quiet, tough labourer receives an honour but is worn down to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: a ghost is literally what remains of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a ghost, the insubstantial shade left of someone who once lived.

clue.text: After beginning, was first to be frightened

indicators.note: After places the next piece behind the one it follows in the clue, as the second half

parts.note: a beginning is a start
someone who was first led the field

explanation.surface: Someone who led from the start of a race but got a scare.
explanation.definitionFit: Being startled is being suddenly alarmed, a close synonym of frightened.

clue.text: Wild partygoers hiding in piece of furniture that can be covered

indicators.note: hiding in says the partygoers are tucked away within the piece of furniture

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture
ravers are people who go to wild parties

explanation.surface: Revellers hiding inside a piece of furniture that can be draped with a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance that can be covered, as on a journey, is distance able to be crossed.

clue.text: Give new status to head of research — agreed after reorganisation

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word research
after reorganisation says the letters of agreed come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A research chief is promoted once a restructuring has been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To regrade is to assign a different grade or rank, which is giving new status.

clue.text: Instruction to players, with time of abstinence over

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Directions to a team now that the fasting season has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is a musical tempo marking telling performers to play slowly.

clue.text: Loses hope, as some French groups of minimal size

parts.note: des is the French word for some
a pair is the smallest possible group, just two

explanation.surface: Someone loses heart because some French parties are so small.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up all hope, the same as to lose it.

clue.text: A hundred and ten gathered round capital's highest point

indicators.note: gathered round says the numerals close in on either side of the capital city

parts.note: C is a hundred and X is ten in Roman numerals
Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A crowd of 110 people gathered around the top of a capital city landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the peak or culmination of something, its highest point.

clue.text: Give chaps solarium treatment for lines?

parts.note: a solarium gives you a tan
chaps are gents, men

explanation.surface: An instruction to send the men off for a sunbed session.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb phrase, 'give chaps solarium treatment' is to tan gents; the question mark signals that the definition is only one kind of line.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry these are straight lines touching a curve at a single point, an example of lines.

clue.text: Place with sect dancing — it's worth seeing

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of both words move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A venue where a religious group dances, said to be well worth a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public show, something that is worth watching.

clue.text: Builders perhaps against having particular vehicles

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
tractors are one particular kind of vehicle

explanation.surface: Construction firms objecting to some specific vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders are one example of contractors, firms hired to do work, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pervasive quality conveyed by Celia, romantically

indicators.note: conveyed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An air or atmosphere carried about by a girl named Celia in her romantic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively an aroma is a subtle pervading character or atmosphere, like a scent that fills a room.

clue.text: Men dress and end up looking silly for poet

indicators.note: looking silly suggests these words are jumbled into a foolish new arrangement

explanation.surface: Men putting on clothes and ending up looking ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link joining the two lots of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: One's 'not standing' for this!

parts.note: sounds like someone refusing to tolerate a thing, but describes someone who is literally not standing, sitting down

explanation.surface: An indignant person declaring they won't put up with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not standing for' usually means refusing to tolerate; here it is literal, sitting rather than standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary means seated or inactive, the condition of someone not on their feet.

clue.text: Forecasts from newspaper folk, with time being limited

indicators.note: being limited says the time is hemmed in on both sides by the journalists

parts.note: the press are journalists collectively
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Predictions made by journalists under tight time pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or portend, so the verb is a synonym of forecasts.

clue.text: Socialist is given praise — lauded finally for showing what he wants wealth to be?

definitions.text: what he wants wealth to be?

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist
a tribute is an act of praise

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word lauded

explanation.surface: A left-winger is praised and honoured for his views on sharing out wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: A socialist wants wealth shared out again more evenly among the people, which is the definition's idea.

clue.text: Attempt to get everyone to eat onion

indicators.note: to eat says the attempt swallows the word for everyone

parts.note: a shot is an attempt
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Trying to get everybody to eat an onion.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small, mild kind of onion.

clue.text: Row? Mark has hesitation to join in

indicators.note: to join in says the hesitation enters the middle of the mark

parts.note: a trace is a mark left behind
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An argument erupts as Mark hesitates to take part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a row of houses; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, a common British street form.

clue.text: In hot weather we may have this warning message

definitions.text: In hot weather we may have this
definitions.meaning: in summer heat we wear fewer clothes, read as two words
a cautionary example or moral that warns someone

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits as LESS ON: what we have on in a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be an experience that serves as a warning, as in 'let that be a lesson'.

clue.text: Buddhist literature giving us art that's extraordinary

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual new order

explanation.surface: Buddhist texts offering us remarkable art.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutras are the scriptural discourses of the Buddha, a body of Buddhist writing.

clue.text: Any number will wear long garment in this island country

indicators.note: will wear says the number is clothed inside the garment

parts.note: a toga is a long robe worn in ancient Rome
N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Lots of people dressed in robes in a Pacific island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom made up of islands in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Authority allows funny man to join African party in church

indicators.note: in says the comic and the party sit within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Edward Lear was the comic writer of nonsense verse
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: An official body permits a comedian to join a South African political party inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission or authorisation, as with security clearance.

clue.text: Nerve centre workers needing person of courage

parts.note: a gang is a group of labourers
a brave person is called a lion

explanation.surface: Workers at a command hub needing someone brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically a ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells, literally a centre of nerves.

clue.text: The old man clumsily handles fruit

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
to paw is to handle something clumsily

explanation.surface: Dad fumbling with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaws, or pawpaws, are tropical fruits, another name for papayas.

clue.text: Most clever male beasts about to face ordeal

indicators.note: about turns the word for the animals round to read the other way

parts.note: rams are male sheep
a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: The brightest male animals are about to undergo a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of', but it turns RAMS into SMAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartest is the superlative of smart, meaning clever.

clue.text: African is keen, having surrendered heart to Irish songstress

indicators.note: the word keen gives up its central pair of letters and the singer takes their place

parts.note: Enya is the Irish singer of Orinoco Flow

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic fan who lost their heart to an Irish singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a person from Kenya, a country of East Africa, so an African.
